overview.title: Humedales y aves en el estuario del Souss
overview.p1: The Souss River mouth and the Souss-Massa National Park coast host wetlands where flamingos and other waterbirds feed. It is a different side of the Agadir region — quieter, more natural, and worth a half-day if you care about wildlife.
overview.p2: Bring binoculars if you have them. Access points vary; a local driver or nature guide helps reach the better viewpoints without disturbing the birds.

food.title: Eat on a birding trip
food.p1: Facilities are limited near the best viewpoints — pack water and snacks, then eat properly back in Agadir or at a coastal café on the return.
food.li2: Simple cafés on the main roads.
food.li3: Full meal on return to the city.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Taxi or guided nature trip from Agadir. Agree the itinerary and waiting time.

2.title: Respect wildlife
2.desc: Keep distance from nesting and feeding birds; stay on paths where marked.

3.title: Gear
3.desc: Binoculars, hat, SPF and closed shoes for rough ground.

q1.question: Can I see flamingos near Agadir?
q1.answer: Yes — the Souss estuary and nearby wetlands are known for flamingos and other waterbirds, with numbers varying by season.

q2.question: Do I need a guide?
q2.answer: Helpful for finding the best access points and identifying species, but not mandatory for a simple viewpoint visit.

q3.question: How far from the city?
q3.answer: The estuary area is roughly 30–60 minutes from central Agadir depending on the exact site.

q4.question: Best season for birds?
q4.answer: Migration periods (broadly autumn and spring) are richest; winter also brings visitors.

q5.question: Is it inside the national park?
q5.answer: Parts of the experience overlap with Souss-Massa National Park — follow park rules where posted.
